THE MONEY SYSTEM

Subjects worth sourcing for `N1` when it is picked up (a wish list, not a plan): closed-loop and zero-export waste systems · thermal treatment and what the residue actually is · materials recovery in isolated and island communities · the energy cost of treatment, since energy is the binding constraint everywhere else in this setting · ⭐ and the social half — whether handling the stream is an obligation, a trade, or a caste-forming job, which is where the culture is.

Ice shelf glaciology — why a station needs to move at all
Political science of figurehead/ceremonial authority

Urban agglomeration / city-merger studies — how two settlements become one metro area
Unplanned megacity growth dynamics

Strategic literature on contested transport chokepoints
Intermodal freight logistics engineering
Company-town / rotational (FIFO) labor sociology
Child development in isolated institutional settings

History of census/vital-records systems and their political weight
Strategic vulnerability of small, concentrated islands

Hedonic/pleasure-city urban planning history
Historiography of single inciting incidents that trigger wars (comparable to WWI assassination literature)

Distributed manufacturing and redundant factory siting

Remote-island supply-chain fragility and logistics
Cold-climate bridge engineering

Highway logistics network design
Controlled-environment/greenhouse agriculture in extreme climates — real Antarctic/Arctic greenhouse research is directly and immediately relevant given the settled breadbasket identity
Limnology and lake-sediment paleoclimate reconstruction — ties directly to Davis's own established lake-science research culture
History of genuinely multi-disciplinary research institutions
High-altitude, extreme-cold engineering — the real Kunlun Station is China's highest Antarctic station
Post-national community formation — craft-guild/professional-identity sociology as a substitute for national identity
Postcolonial identity reclamation — communities reclaiming an externally-imposed founding myth as genuinely their own
Textile/fashion arts history tied to research and education culture
Large-scale advanced/additive manufacturing systems
Sociology of communities that existed before being formally named (statelessness/undocumented community literature)
Subglacial lake science — the real Lake Vostok is one of the most-studied subglacial lakes on Earth, extremely rich source material (extremophile biology, drilling-contamination protocols)
Extremophile biology — life in extreme cold, sealed ecosystems
Communities built around inherited records — living with logs, journals and maps left by people they never met
Buffer-state / small-power-between-two-larger-neighbors geopolitics
Cultural continuity and refinement (rather than change) over generations
Katabatic-wind-resistant shielded architecture
Real Cape Adare/Borchgrevink expedition history — the actual first overwintering site in Antarctica
Adélie penguin colony ecology — Cape Adare hosts one of the largest real colonies on the continent
Acoustic/community music culture
Extreme wind engineering — the real Cape Denison is the windiest place at sea level on Earth (Mawson's original expedition site); directly worth researching
Fused megastructure architecture for extreme climates
Small-island siting and sea-ice access on the Adélie coast — the real Petrel Island site's physical conditions
Human-wildlife coexistence urban planning — the real station routes infrastructure around penguin colonies already
Active-volcano hazard engineering and civil defense — Mt. Erebus is a real, active volcano near the real McMurdo Station
Political geography of informal-to-formal capital transitions
Preserved historic polar huts — the real Scott/Terra Nova hut is an actual heritage site, direct existing parallel
Small-town-next-to-metropolis sociology
Sister-city/twin-settlement sociology
The real site's physical conditions at Mawson's coordinates — terrain, wind, sea-ice access
Founder-population demographic drift and replacement sociology
Real Dome Fuji ice-core science — deep ice-core drilling and paleoclimate records, rich source material
Sacralization of scientific/technical sites — real literature on research sites becoming pilgrimage destinations
Crossroads/waystation town sociology
Island-junction logistics — East Ongul Island's sea-ice and overland access to the mainland
Subterranean/under-ice city engineering
Heavy industrial robotics fabrication from raw materials
Antarctic Treaty neutrality as a governance model — the treaty's own provisions, not any station's operating history
Space elevator / space-fountain engineering theory — directly ties to the existing Amundsen Tower project notes
